rows.sourceTitle: Lymphedema and Post-Operative Complications after Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy versus Lymphadenectomy in Endometrial Carcinomas-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.claimType: treatment-mediated lower-extremity lymphedema after lymphatic-disrupting nodal treatment for endometrial cancer
rows.proposition: In endometrial carcinoma, pelvic or para-aortic lymph-node dissection is associated with lower-extremity lymphedema; the approved mapping is restricted to treatment-mediated lymphedema after lymphatic-disrupting nodal treatment.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: treatment-mediated lower-extremity lymphedema after pelvic/para-aortic lymphatic-disrupting nodal treatment
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented endometrial cancer, pelvic or para-aortic lymphatic-disrupting nodal treatment, and separately established lower-extremity lymphedema afterward. Do not infer lymphedema from endometrial cancer alone or from isolated edema. Preserve deep-vein thrombosis or other venous disease, cardiac or renal edema, primary lymphedema, infection, and other unrelated causes as competing explanations.
rows.citation: Helgers RJA, Winkens B, Slangen BFM, Werner HMJ. Lymphedema and Post-Operative Complications after Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy versus Lymphadenectomy in Endometrial Carcinomas-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Clin Med. 2020;10(1):120. PMID 33396373. doi:10.3390/jcm10010120.

rows.sourceTitle: Best evidence for rehabilitation management of urinary incontinence in patients with bladder cancer following orthotopic neobladder reconstruction
rows.claimType: treatment-mediated urinary incontinence after radical cystectomy with orthotopic neobladder reconstruction
rows.proposition: The evidence synthesis addresses urinary incontinence after radical cystectomy with orthotopic neobladder reconstruction for bladder cancer; the approved mapping is restricted to that postoperative treatment pathway.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: persistent urinary incontinence after radical cystectomy with orthotopic neobladder reconstruction for bladder cancer
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented bladder cancer, radical cystectomy with orthotopic neobladder reconstruction, and persistent separately established postoperative urinary incontinence. Do not infer urinary incontinence from bladder cancer alone, from an ileal conduit without the phenotype, or from transient early postoperative leakage. Preserve urinary tract infection, retention or overflow, neurologic or pelvic-floor disease, preexisting urinary incontinence, and other etiologies as competing explanations.
rows.citation: Xu M, Chen S, Liu X, et al. Best evidence for rehabilitation management of urinary incontinence in patients with bladder cancer following orthotopic neobladder reconstruction. Asia Pac J Oncol Nurs. 2024;12:100647. PMID 39896758. doi:10.1016/j.apjon.2024.100647.

rows.sourceTitle: Aspects of vincristine-induced neuropathy in hematologic malignancies: a systematic review
rows.claimType: treatment-mediated peripheral neuropathy after vincristine-containing or otherwise specifically neurotoxic lymphoma treatment
rows.proposition: Vincristine used for hematologic malignancies, including non-Hodgkin lymphoma, can cause progressive peripheral sensory and motor neuropathy; the approved mapping is restricted to a documented neurotoxic treatment exposure with compatible chronology.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: treatment-mediated peripheral neuropathy after documented vincristine-containing or otherwise specifically neurotoxic lymphoma regimen
rows.publicationGuard: Require documented non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a documented vincristine-containing or otherwise specifically neurotoxic lymphoma regimen, compatible chronology, and separately established peripheral neuropathy. Do not infer peripheral neuropathy from non-Hodgkin lymphoma itself. Preserve diabetic, nutritional, alcohol-related, compressive, paraproteinemic, infectious, hereditary, and other neuropathy etiologies as competing explanations.
rows.citation: Madsen ML, Due H, Ejskjaer N, et al. Aspects of vincristine-induced neuropathy in hematologic malignancies: a systematic review. Cancer Chemother Pharmacol. 2019;84(3):471-485. PMID 31214762. doi:10.1007/s00280-019-03884-5.

rows.sourceTitle: Risk Factors for Incontinence-Associated Dermatitis in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.claimType: phenotype-restricted incontinence-associated dermatitis from repeated or prolonged fecal exposure
rows.proposition: A systematic review and meta-analysis identifies fecal incontinence as an etiologic risk factor for incontinence-associated dermatitis; the approved mapping is restricted to moisture-associated skin damage in the exposed distribution.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: incontinence-associated dermatitis in the perineal or other directly exposed distribution
rows.publicationGuard: Require fecal incontinence with repeated or prolonged perineal skin exposure and separately diagnosed moisture-associated or incontinence-associated dermatitis in the exposed distribution. Do not generalize this relationship to eczema, fungal disease, allergic or irritant dermatitis from unrelated agents, pressure injury, cellulitis, or a nonspecific rash. Preserve those alternative skin diagnoses and other causes as competing explanations.
rows.citation: Jiang T, Zhang X, Wu J, Gao L, Tung TH. Risk Factors for Incontinence-Associated Dermatitis in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Wound Ostomy Continence Nurs. 2025;52(1):66-75. PMID 39836004. doi:10.1097/WON.0000000000001146.

rows.sourceTitle: Outcome of Anterior and Posterior Endoscopic Procedures for Cervical Radiculopathy Due to Degenerative Disk Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
rows.claimType: anatomically concordant cervical radiculopathy due to cervical degenerative disc disease with nerve-root compromise
rows.proposition: The systematic review and meta-analysis explicitly addresses cervical radiculopathy due to degenerative disc disease; the approved mapping is restricted to anatomically concordant cervical nerve-root disease.
rows.phenotypeRestriction: cervical degenerative disc disease with anatomically concordant cervical radiculopathy
rows.publicationGuard: Require cervical degenerative disc pathology capable of nerve-root compromise and separately established anatomically concordant cervical radiculopathy. Do not infer radiculopathy from degenerative imaging, axial neck pain, nonspecific paresthesias, myelopathy, or peripheral entrapment neuropathy alone. Preserve peripheral neuropathy, plexopathy, entrapment neuropathy, spinal cord disease, nondegenerative structural lesions, and other causes as competing explanations.
rows.citation: Alomar SA, Maghrabi Y, Baeesa SS, Alves OL. Outcome of Anterior and Posterior Endoscopic Procedures for Cervical Radiculopathy Due to Degenerative Disk Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Global Spine J. 2022;12(7):1546-1560. PMID 34402323. doi:10.1177/21925682211037270.
